title: Deglue dispatcher: split continuous queue, async KV priming, scheduler coordinator simplification
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem:
The continuous enqueue/dispatcher code has accreted multiple responsibilities over the last 18 months: slot allocation, KV prefetching, batching lane management, and backpressure heuristics. This "glued" design makes it hard to reason about latency vs cost trade-offs, results in several lock-contention hotspots during peak traffic, and complicates KV cache warmup (we see long tails when shards are cold).

Goal:
Split the dispatcher into three bounded-concurrency subsystems to reduce contention, make KV warmup explicit and observable, and simplify the scheduler coordinator so it no longer holds a global epoch mutex during commit. Primary goals are to reduce p95 latency for short sessions, lower end-to-end variance, and make the KV prefetch behavior configurable per-customer.

Scope / Non-goals:
- Do: 1) Extract async KV priming service (prefetcher) from dispatcher; 2) Replace monolithic slot allocator with coordinator that uses occupancy counters and CAS-free handoff; 3) Introduce feature flag deglue_dispatcher and a canary policy for traffic percentage; 4) Add metrics and dashboards for kv_prefetch_hit_ratio, batch_coalesce_latency_p50/p95, scheduler_contention_count.
- Don't: Rework model kernels or GPU drivers. Multi-node shard redistribution is out of scope for this ticket (will be followed up).

Design summary:
- Dispatcher -> Dispatcher-lite (ingest + routing only).
- Prefetcher: background worker pool with bounded goroutines, per-shard token budget, backpressure when memory budget exceeded. Exposes control plane hooks to set per-customer prefetch strategy (none, eager, on-demand).
- Scheduler coordinator: epoch-less commit path. Use per-slot sequencers and occupancy counters to allow lock-free transfer when possible; fall back to fast-path CAS when contention detected.
- Observability: add tracing spans for prefetch lifecycle, KV priming latency histogram, and slot handoff counters.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit/integration tests for dispatcher-lite, prefetcher, and coordinator exist and pass in CI.
- Canary on runtime-1.20 reduces p95 latency for 0-128 token sessions by >= 12% on average across our internal benchmark set (chat-short).
- KV prefetch hit ratio observable and default strategy set to "on-demand" for hosted tenants; document how to switch to "eager" on Dedicated customers.
- No increase in tail OOMs during canary (memory delta <= +10% baseline).
- Feature flag deglue_dispatcher allows rollback within 2 minutes via console route.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Prefetcher may increase memory usage under skewed hot-key traffic. Mitigation: per-shard budget + eviction token to throttle prefetch; canary with 5% traffic and automated rollback if memory exceeds threshold.
- Risk: Removing global epoch could expose rare reordering. Mitigation: implement fast-path assertions and a small safety window (50ms) during rollout; schedule a follow-up formal verification if assertion fires > 3 times in 24h.

Open questions:
- Parameterization: optimal prefetch budget per-shard needs A/B tuning (initial default 64KB steady-state).
- Operator UX: whether to expose prefetch strategy on the per-customer Console page or keep it advanced-only.

Links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Deglue+Dispatcher+RFC (internal)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345 (prefetcher POC)

implementation_notes: Key implementation choices: 1) Prefetcher uses bounded goroutine pool with token-bucket per-shard; 2) Coordinator uses per-slot sequencer to avoid global locks; 3) Dispatcher-lite is single-threaded per-core and only routes to lanes. Feature flag is implemented in config-service with fast rollback hook. Tests include chaos: kv-shard-restart scenario and high-hotkey pressure.
postmortem_plan: If canary fails (p95 regression or memory >10%), immediately flip feature flag off, capture heap profile and kv metrics, roll back coordinator change first. Follow-up PR will add adaptive prefetch budget and eviction backpressure if needed.

owner_notes: This ticket targets a strategic simplification: by pulling KV priming out of the hot path we expect to make future batching experiments much simpler. Keep PRs small and focused; aim for 2-3 incremental merges rather than one large rewrite.
